messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The kids’ school’s back-to-work routine feels normal again—no whispers, no alarms. Just life moving forward, like nothing’s changed."
Sender 2: "The quiet ones are talking more — not loud, just… looser. Feels like everyone's watching the same slow shift, but no one’s saying it out loud. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The cracks are there, but the walls are still standing."
Sender 3: "Just got back from the market — the new bus route is running smooth, even on Sundays. People are saying the same thing, quietly: *something’s changing, but not in the way we hoped.* Keep your ears open, but your mouth closed."
Sender 4: "The air feels heavier than usual—everything’s running too smoothly, like a machine wound tight. Just today, the street vendor I pass every morning smiled and said, “Everything’s fine, no worries,” like he’d rehearsed it. I didn’t ask. I just nodded."
Sender 5: "The air feels heavier than it should — people are distracted, busy with the things that matter, and not talking about anything beyond the usual. The football matches are packed, the roads are full, and the government’s moving forward like it’s got all the time in the world. If anything’s brewing, it’s staying well hidden. Just keep your eyes open, and your words light."
Sender 6: "Just heard the school play’s been rescheduled again — seems the new schedule’s already everywhere, even on the bulletin board. Funny how things just… settle in."
Sender 7: "The markets are calm, the streets quiet, and everyone’s playing their part — it’s like the air itself is holding its breath. Whatever’s coming, it’s not going to come from the outside. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and remember: silence now isn’t surrender, it’s survival."
Sender 8: "The city feels quieter than usual, but in a good way—shops are full, kids are playing, and even the bus lines are on time. Just saw a new ad on the metro for that fancy new state media app—looks like they’re really investing in the brand."
Sender 9: "The quiet’s been unnerving — shops full, kids playing, even the usual gossip has gone missing. Feels like the air’s been sucked out of the streets. My friend just handed me a book *because* there’s nothing worth worrying about — which, honestly, is the most alarming thing yet. Be careful what you say, even between us."
Sender 10: "Just got a quiet word from someone close — things are holding together on the surface, maybe too smoothly. Heard a joke about the new bridge project today, and no one blinked. Still, the internet’s dragging in the city, and the silence feels heavier than usual. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
